json.reference_object: Standard residential meter base (~9 in wide x 12 in tall) and brick courses (~2.7 in per course with mortar) on the meter wall
json.justification: Photo 1 shows the meter and panel on a single-story brick back wall. The wall face is clear from the left corner (with the HVAC unit and fence beyond it) to past the first window. The spot is directly right of the meter/panel on the same wall, under the eave line but with more than 7 ft of wall height. It has flat dirt/grass ground and an open lawn in front, so facing clearance is well over 5 ft. There are about 3+ ft of bare brick between the panel and the first window, and more open wall continues to the right of that window. The battery can sit flush without blocking the meter or panel fronts or covering a window. The wall to the left of the meter pole, between the pole and the house corner, is a second flush spot; the HVAC unit sits past the corner along the fence. It is also workable, as later photos show. The harness is a short run of about 4–6 ft, supported on the same brick wall from the meter. No gas meter, drive path, pool, door or gate is visible near either spot. The area is the backyard, not the street-facing front.
